prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy review/prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Medication Order Gateway (validates orders from clinical systems; flags missing/duplicate/conflicting data; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot; provides current order status; routes to review). Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot (prepares authorized orders; Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents package to Verification Station). Pharmacy Verification Station (final check; records outcome; blocks release if checks incomplete; produces Batch Release Note). Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler (temperature records while awaiting transfer; reports excursions, connectivity loss). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (East checks/reports route availability; monitors capsules; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket on deviation/timeout). Pneumatic Tube Network (accepts only compliant packaged/routed loads; segment unavailable until tested). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (states Ready for Dispense, Out of Service blocks dispensing). Medication Return Kiosk (Return Bin Audit Label). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (reviews clinical/labeling exceptions; documents concern disposition; Dose Exception Review Slip). Pharmacy Technician (prep; confirms contents/patient IDs match order; Cold Chain Handoff Card). Medication Safety Officer (Diversion Review Packet). Registered Nurse. Charge Nurse (Cabinet Downtime Notice). Hospital Courier (checks count/integrity/destination/handling; records acceptance time/identity; produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; verifies capsule closed). Biomedical Engineer, IT Operations Specialist, dispatch/operations staff. Requirements: discrepancies block prep; release only after order/medication/destination checked vs instructions; release linked to order ID, package ID, time, staff credentials; canceled/duplicate/superseded requests held, not loaded; manifest lists packages, destinations, handling, assembly time; IDs checked vs manifest; cold items controlled until custody transfer; excursion/returns segregated; cabinet unavailable until Ready for Dispense and checks done; operations closes interruption after workflows confirmed; dispatch resumes after checks and authorization; fault/corrective action/verification recorded.

New part:
S095: Before a capsule is admitted, its package identifiers and destination are reconciled with the prepared load information.
S096: A route or packaging problem places the load on hold until staff resolve the condition and document the outcome.
S097: If automated transfer is unavailable, staff retain custody and use an approved alternate delivery procedure.
S098: The receiving department confirms arrival and reports any discrepancy through the established operational process.
S099: Ward staff perform a receipt check on each arriving load before placing medication in a cabinet or transferring custody.
S100: A Registered Nurse or other authorized ward staff member verifies that the load is intended for the ward.
S101: North Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the north ward.
S102: South Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the south ward.
S103: North Ward Cabinet Controller uses the Priority Refill Tote Tag to confirm the intended ward before staff accept a tote.
S104: Staff inspect the outer packaging for damage, moisture, tampering, or other signs that the load may be unsafe to handle.
S105: Ward staff compare package identifiers with the cabinet task list and confirm that the identifiers are legible.
S106: Cabinet staff verify the quantity and medication descriptions against the expected receipt record.
S107: For refrigerated medication, a Registered Nurse checks that the load remained within the required handling conditions.
S108: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler displays the current temperature and any recorded excursion for staff review.
S109: Staff isolate a load when its identity, quantity, packaging, or temperature condition does not match the expected receipt.
S110: Staff do not place an unresolved load into active cabinet stock.
S111: Accepted medication is staged in the designated receiving area until cabinet placement is authorized.
S112: The ward records receipt completion and any discrepancy through the established operational process.
S113: Ward staff check return bins before use to confirm that each bin is intact, clean, and assigned to the correct return stream.
S114: A Registered Nurse confirms that the contents are eligible for return and are separated from waste and non-medication items.
S115: Staff check that each return bin closes securely and that its contents do not obstruct the closure.
S116: Tallowmere guides ward staff through return-bin checks and records each check outcome for follow-up.
S117: The Pharmacy Technician uses the audit label to identify a return bin for the scheduled collection.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
